# This file is autogenerated by pip-compile with Python 3.12
# by the following command:
#
#    pip-compile -o requirements.txt requirements.in
#
# Hand-patched after generation: pip-tools resolves this lock on the compiling
# host (macOS) only, and does not carry over the platform markers that some
# of these packages declare on their own conditional dependencies (checked
# via each package's own Requires-Dist metadata). Two instances are known and
# patched below:
#   - pystray depends on pyobjc-framework-quartz only when
#     sys_platform == "darwin"; without the marker, `pip install -r
#     requirements.txt` fails outright on Linux (PyObjC does not build
#     there) — this is exactly what broke the container image (see
#     requirements-docker.txt).
#   - pystray depends on python-xlib only when sys_platform == "linux";
#     without the marker it is missing from the lock entirely, so a Linux
#     install (the container's platform) floats it to whatever version
#     PyPI serves that day, defeating the point of pinning.
# This list is not closed — any platform-conditional transitive dependency
# is at risk the same way (e.g. click depends on colorama only on Windows;
# not added here because no Windows build exists yet, but watch for it when
# one does). tests/test_requirements_lock.py enforces the markers below so a
# future `pip-compile` re-run that silently drops them fails the suite
# instead of failing quietly on the next platform someone tries.
